assessments.reasoning: The organisation's own site states plainly that it accepts zakat and holds it in a designated account (E1), the narrative repeats it (E2), and it describes administering zakat against a one-eighth ceiling on zakat received (E3), which is the kind of zakat-specific policy the criterion asks for. Confidence is held below the ceiling because every item is the organisation's own unaudited representation about itself.

The narrative describes fees, materials and monthly cash stipends reaching means-tested poor households in the haor basin (E8, E9), which is in-kind and cash support to people below a locally-assessed sufficiency threshold and so matches fuqara_masakin. E10 shows the registered purpose leads with advancing education, but a charity may pursue relief of poverty through schooling costs and that does not displace the fit.

The organisation states zakat sits in a designated account, is not pooled and is not spent on unrestricted costs (E1, E4), and the enrolment pack shows the operational consequence — households failing the zakat screen are paid from general donations and recorded separately (E5). The criterion is satisfied by a statement of segregated accounting, though the statement is self-reported and no bank or audit record corroborates it.

A documented zakat eligibility screen with nisab and duplicate-receipt tests is applied before zakat is released, described on the site (E6) and reproduced as Part 2 of the enrolment instrument with a screener signature line (E7). That is a documented screening process rather than a bare assertion that screening happens.

Fees are paid per named pupil against a countersigned ledger rather than as a block grant (E11, E12) and stipends go by mobile money to a named household member (E13), so the money is traceable to identified households. E14 and E15 show head office rent and a contested field-staff classification consuming between 6% and 12.8% of the appeal, which is ordinary overhead alongside beneficiary payments rather than funding of a general operating budget.

There is a written means test with quantitative income, land and schooling thresholds applied in the household rather than at the school (E16, E17, E18), and continuing need is re-verified twice yearly with recorded continue/suspend/investigate outcomes for all 410 households (E19). This is documented local vetting, not an assurance that vetting occurs.

The narrative states outright that stipends and fee payments are grants and that no family repays anything (E20), and nothing in the budget describes a loan, equity or repayment term. E21 describes recovery of unspent fees from the school when a pupil leaves, which is a clawback against the institution rather than a repayment obligation on the household, so it does not cut against the criterion.
